extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of a social-progress literary magazine; women interested in social reform, book reviewers, and general literary readers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative criteria and expressive standards for reviewing and describing books, essays, and fiction in a progressive women's literary magazine — focusing on clarity, tone, evidence, focus, and stylistic qualities such as wit and workmanship.

rubrics_metrics.name: plain_simple_moderate_language
rubrics_metrics.description: “The work deals in the main, in plain, simple moderate language...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor clear, straightforward diction and a moderate register when addressing a broad public; avoid overly technical, ornate, or sensational language so the subject (here, pathological aspects and social implications) is accessible to general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: effective_title_links_topics
rubrics_metrics.description: “The title is a good one, for it links two aspects of one subject, and presents the new case without ignoring the old one.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a title that signals the book's scope and balance — linking related aspects and indicating both novelty and continuity. A good title frames reader expectations and shows the author's balanced approach to new and established views.

rubrics_metrics.name: clear_descriptions_and_statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: “The first part gives clear descriptions of the venereal diseases... giving statistics as to their prevalence.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide lucid, concrete descriptions of phenomena and back claims with prevalence statistics or quantitative data where possible. Clarity and empirical support increase credibility, especially on medical or social subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: appropriate_emphasis_in_treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: “laying stress not so much upon the moral danger, long known, as on the physical danger, to which we are but just awakening.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately choose what aspect to emphasize (e.g., physical vs moral consequences) according to the author's purpose and the readers' needs; justify shifts in emphasis when addressing new evidence or perspectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: use_of_scientific_authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: “giving a long list of scientific authorities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support arguments with citations to recognized scientific authorities and sources. A substantial bibliography or list of consulted experts bolsters the work's authority and persuasiveness, particularly in nonfiction dealing with health or social science.

rubrics_metrics.name: moderate_tone
rubrics_metrics.description: “It is a clean, forcible interesting book, most moderate in tone; and giving a long list of scientific authorities.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a measured tone — firm and persuasive without sensationalism or moral hysteria. Moderation helps convey seriousness and reach a wider audience while preserving credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: practical_prevention_and_hopeful_guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: “The third part discusses Prevention; with wise and hopeful words; telling how chance infection may be avoided...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonfiction that treats social or medical ills should include practical, actionable prevention advice and a constructive, hopeful outlook where appropriate. Readers value concrete guidance they can apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: stay_on_theme_coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: “Her special matter in discussion is exactly given in the title, and she does not stray from her theme;”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain focus and coherence: a book should pursue the topic announced in its title and not diverge into unrelated territory. Tight thematic discipline strengthens the argument and reader satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: trenchant_wit_and_penetrating_satire
rubrics_metrics.description: “A keen and accurate weapon is Miss Hamilton's pen... uses it with delicious dexterity to prick bubbles... The amusing quality is for those who like trenchant wit and penetrating satire.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For satirical or polemical writing, aim for incisive, sharply argued wit that exposes absurdities without descending into mere invective. Effective satire is precise, focused, and dexterous in its targets and techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: clever_and_forcible_argument
rubrics_metrics.description: “This is 'Marriage as a Trade,' by Cicely Hamilton... A keen and accurate weapon is Miss Hamilton's pen; and in this work she uses it with delicious dexterity to prick bubbles, to slice off masks, cut veils and bandages, and dissect ancient idols.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate argumentative writing on the basis of cleverness and force: does the author deploy rhetorical tools to expose assumptions and dismantle falsehoods? Praise when the prose is both intellectually sharp and energetically delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: workmanship_in_fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: “Mary Jonston is a writer of good novels, strong, thrilling, excellent in workmanship...”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess fiction for technical craftsmanship: plot construction, pacing, tension, characterization, and prose control. 'Workmanship' denotes the visible skill with which the novel is built and sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: author_reputation_as_indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: “as all who have read her 'To Have and To Hold' will agree;”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an author's prior successful works as contextual evidence for evaluating new publications, while still assessing each work on its own merits. Reputation can inform expectations but should not substitute for fresh evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: audience_specific_relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: “As each of these diseases affects both wife and child, it is specially necessary that women should be informed about them.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether a work serves the informational needs of its intended audience. In advocacy or educational writing, tailor content to the specific concerns and roles of the target readership (here, women and mothers).

rubrics_metrics.name: value_for_price_and_pocket-size_usefulness
rubrics_metrics.description: “'To‑day's Problems' is a good ten cents' worth--or five, if you live in Chicago. It is a pocket-size pamphlet, full of short bits... And not a thing in it that fills one page, even.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For pamphlets and brief collections evaluate practical value relative to price and portability: usefulness, variety, and accessibility matter for readers seeking concise, actionable ideas.
